title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, Guardrails, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied ML evaluation practices for model onboarding, prompt set & benchmark management, guardrails, quantization profile definition, and regression triage. It is the canonical cross-team runbook used by Applied ML, Serving Runtime, and Platform to:
- Reduce onboarding time for new models and variants.
- Prevent production regressions via automated evals and structured triage.
- Provide repeatable quantization checks that preserve quality & latency targets.
- Ensure prompt sets and benchmarks reflect real customer workloads.

Scope
Applies to: hosted Redwood API models, Dedicated model variants, and Private deployment builds. Includes curated open-source models and internally fine-tuned variants. Excludes experimental research prototypes (those remain in research notebooks until promoted).

Ownership and Contacts
- Document owner: Applied ML (Aisha Patel)
- Primary executors: Applied ML Engineers, Model Onboarding SREs
- Escalation: Serving Runtime oncall -> Eng SRE -> Head of Applied ML
- Slack channels: #applied-ml, #model-onboarding, #eval-harness

Terminology
- Eval harness: the centralized CI system that runs unit/benchmark/eval suites against model checkpoints.
- Prompt set: curated input examples representing a workload slice (e.g., customer-support, code-complete).
- Benchmark: aggregated metrics across prompt sets and model variants.
- QR (Quality Regression): any measurable decline vs baseline on a tracked metric.
- Quant profile: named config with precision, backend, and kernel flags for a model variant.

High-level Process (summary)
1. Model intake and triage
   - Submit a Model Onboarding Request (MOR) in the onboarding tracker with intended use cases, dataset links, and target latency/cost SLOs.
2. Eval harness baseline
   - Run unit tests + prompt-set benchmarks using the eval harness. Record baseline metrics.
3. Quantization and perf pass
   - Generate candidate quant profiles; run quantization evals with automated acceptance checks.
4. Guardrails & canarying
   - Configure quality guardrails; run canary rollout in staging with live traffic sampling.
5. Regression monitoring
   - Post-deploy, monitor eval runs and production metrics; if regression detected, follow triage playbook.

Detailed Procedures

A. Eval Harness Onboarding Checklist
Follow these steps when adding a new model to the eval harness (MUST):
1) Pre-checks (owner completes)
   - Confirm license & compliance status (legal/team).
   - Provide model artifact URI (S3/GCS) and checksum.
   - Target sequence lengths and expected latency percentile targets.

2) Implement harness integration (Applied ML engineer)
   - Add model config under /configs/models/<model-name>.yaml with fields: architecture, vocab, context_size, tokenizer, backend_compat.
   - Implement a lightweight inference adapter (Python) that exposes run_inference(inputs, config). See example below.

3) Baseline runs (CI)
   - Run unit tests: tokenizer sanity, deterministic seed checks.
   - Run prompt-set suite (see section B). Save baseline run id and commit to model metadata.

4) Review & sign-off
   - Applied ML lead and Serving Runtime reviewer must sign-off in MOR before quantization or canarying.

Code snippet: python adapter (example)
```python
# minimal adapter used by the eval harness
import json
from runtime_client import LocalModel

model = LocalModel(uri="s3://models/model-v1.tar.gz")

def run_inference(batch_inputs, config):
    # config: dict with decode params
    return model.generate(batch_inputs, max_tokens=config.get('max_tokens', 64))
```

B. Prompt Sets and Benchmark Guidelines
Purpose: ensure prompt sets are stable, representative, and versioned.

Prompt set lifecycle
- Collection: Product/SEs collect real examples (anonymized) + synthetic augmentations.
- Curation: Applied ML curators create slices (intent, domain, length bucket).
- Versioning: Store prompt sets in the prompt catalog with semantic versioning (vMAJOR.MINOR).
- Ownership: Each prompt set must list an owner and a use-case label.

Minimum prompt set requirements
- Size: 200 samples per slice for categorical tasks; 1k for open-generation workloads.
- Labels: gold-standard label or rubric for quality scoring (where applicable).
- Metadata: source, date-collected, anonymization method, tags.

Benchmark execution cadence
- Pre-merge: Run a quick smoke benchmark (10% sample) on PR.
- Integration CI: Full benchmark on mainline model additions and quant profile changes.
- Nightly: Run critical prompt sets for top 10 customers & synthetic safety sets.

Example benchmark table (metrics to record):
| metric | description | pass threshold | owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| ROUGE-L | overlap for summarization slices | >= 0.72 (vs baseline) | Applied ML |
| Exact Match | QA classification correctness | >= 95% | Applied ML |
| Toxicity Score | avg toxicity (detector) | <= baseline + 0.02 | Safety |
| Latency p95 | 95th percentile server latency | <= 250ms | Serving Runtime |

C. Quality Guardrails
Guardrails are automated checks that gate rollouts. Configure guardrails in the eval CI config with rule definitions and severity.

Default guardrail rules
- Quality: no metric drop greater than 1.5% absolute vs model baseline on primary benchmark for the target SA (service area).
- Safety: any increase > 0.5% in toxicity or safety fail rate -> block.
- Latency: p95 increase > 20% and > 100ms absolute -> block.
- Cost: per-token cost increase > 10% without commensurate quality improvement -> review.

Guardrail actions
- block: CI fails and deployment prevented.
- warn: CI passes but creates high-priority alert for release owner.
- monitor: record metric and create dashboard annotation.

How to add a guardrail (steps)
1) Define metric and SQL/metric extraction query.
2) Add rule to eval_harness/config/guardrails.yaml with owner and action.
3) Add dashboard tile and alert in Grafana with matching thresholds.
4) Request review from Safety and Serving Runtime.

D. Quantization Profiles and Acceptance Criteria
Quant profiles are treated as first-class artifacts. Each profile includes: precision (e.g., int8, fp16), backend (cuBLAS, Triton-kernel), kernel flags, and simulated perf/cost estimates.

Profile naming convention
- <model>-<variant>-<precision>-<backend>-v<MAJOR> (e.g., llama2-13b-int8-triton-v1)

Automated quantization flow
1) Generate candidate profiles using quant-tooling (see CLI below).
2) Run quant-eval jobs: accuracy benchmark + perf benchmark using identical seeds and prompt sets.
3) Compare to baseline using the acceptance checks.
4) If accepted, register profile in the model registry and schedule a canary rollout.

Quant acceptance checks (must pass all):
- Quality: Aggregate primary metric delta <= 1.0% absolute (or within profile-specific tolerance set by model owner).
- Safety: No increase in flagged examples above baseline (detector threshold).
- Functional: Token-level decode agreement > 98% for deterministically seeded tests.
- Latency: p95 improvement or <= baseline + 10ms (profile should not regress latency severely).

CLI examples
- Generate candidates:
  rwd-quant generate --model s3://models/llama2-13b --out /tmp/quant-candidates
- Run quant eval job (k8s):
  rwd-eval submit --profile /tmp/quant-candidates/int8-triton.yaml --suite prompt-sets/core-v1 --timeout 2h

E. Regression Triage Playbook
Purpose: provide an actionable, time-bounded process when a regression is detected by eval harness or production monitoring.

Severity levels
- Sev1 (critical): Production regressions causing customer-visible failures (e.g., >5% drop in primary metric for top 5 customers or safety incident). Immediate incident process.
- Sev2 (high): Significant metric drop in staging or CI failing guardrails that affects multiple slices. 24-hour initial response.
- Sev3 (medium): Single-slice degradation or minor drift; track and resolve in regular sprint.

Triage steps (ordered)
1) Detect & flag
   - Source: eval harness CI, nightly benchmarks, or prod monitor. Create an issue in the regression tracker with run id, diff, and affected prompt sets.
2) Rapid repro (owner within 2 hours for Sev1/2)
   - Re-run failing suites with identical seeds and full logging. Capture model artifact IDs, quant profile, and runtime config.
3) Scope & isolate
   - Compare recent changes (model checkpoints, quant profiles, tokenizer, runtime flags). Use binary search if needed (bisect model commits).
4) Mitigation decision (within 8 hours for Sev1; 48 hours for Sev2)
   - Options: rollback to baseline artifact, disable quant profile, or serve fallback variant. Document decision and notify stakeholders.
5) Root cause analysis (post-mitigation)
   - Produce RCA document in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage within 5 working days.

Triage checklist (for issue)
- run_id, baseline_run_id, delta_metrics (list)
- model artifact id(s), config hashes
- quant profile name (if used)
- tokenizer version & vocab hash
- runtime kernel flags and backend
- recent infra changes (drivers, CUDA, container images)

F. Canary and Rollout Guidance
- Canary size: 1-5% traffic to new model/quant profile for first 24 hours.
- Traffic ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (typically 24-48h between steps if no alerts).
- Canary metrics: top-level business metric, primary eval metric, p95 latency, error rate, cost estimate.
- Automatic rollback conditions: any Sev1 trigger, or sustained >1.5% primary metric delta for two consecutive evaluation windows (4h each).

G. Dashboards and Alerts (operationalizing)
Required dashboards
- Per-model eval dashboard: baseline vs current run, per-slice breakdown.
- Quant profile comparison dashboard: overlay baseline and quant runs including token-level disagreement heatmap.
- Regression-triage queue: active regressions, owners, status.

Key alerts
- Guardrail-block alert (paging for Sev1).
- Canary deviation alert: primary metric delta > 1% sustained for 2 windows (page for Sev2).
- Nightly-run failure alert: summary CI failure (email + Slack).

H. Templates and Artifacts
Include these templates in the repo:
- MOR template (model intake form)
- Eval run metadata schema (yaml/json)
- Regression issue template (with checklist fields above)
- Quant profile metadata template (include perf estimates and known limitations)

Appendix: Example Eval Run Metadata (yaml inline)
```yaml

model: llama2-13b-v1
profile: llama2-13b-int8-triton-v1
prompt_sets: [core-v1, safety-v1]
metrics:
  rouge_l: 0.731
  exact_match: 0.946
  toxicity_rate: 0.021
latency_p95_ms: 234

notes: "Quant profile introduced minimal decode diffs; accepted by Applied ML"
```
